# Joining hinge stress to base-balanced moment bodies

This note combines two independently proved ingredients without
discarding their remaining multiplier terms:

* `candidate a5428a02cd85fb48` gives a lower bound
  for a weighted cap-hinge sum from an actual whole-fiber cover;
* `candidate de8d1a3251731edd` and
  `candidate d233b11c4a70933f` give attained
  hinge minima and their exact stresses.

Let `D` be the fixed continuous difference body used for normalization,
so `h_D(u_i)=1`. The Euclidean unit-ball normalization is a special case.
For each integer fiber `z`, choose any

`0<t_z<=T_max(z)`

and its actual base-balanced moment body `M_(t_z)(z) subset K_z`.
Suppose that body contains a translate

`p_z+rho_z D subset M_(t_z)(z)`, `rho_z>=0`.                    (1)

No positive uniform lower bound on these radii is presumed.

## 1. The affine-normalized cover-hinge bound

For the attained whole-fiber certificate `lambda_z`, set
`U_z=sum_i lambda_zi u_i` and let `C_z` be its cover margin. The exact
moment-body support dual, applied to each actual cap, gives

`sum_i lambda_zi Psi_i
 >=t_z[C_z+h_Kz(-U_z)+sum_i lambda_zi h_Mtz(ui)]`.

This is the support-dual inequality from the referenced cover-hinge note
with the integer tilt centered at `z`; changing `b_i` to `b_i-a_i dot z`
does not change the actual cap or hinge. By (1) and `h_D(u_i)=1`,

`sum_i lambda_zi h_Mtz(u_i)>=U_z dot p_z+rho_z`.

Also `p_z in K_z`, so `h_Kz(-U_z)>=-U_z dot p_z`. Consequently

`sum_i lambda_zi Psi_i>=t_z(C_z+rho_z)`.                       (2)

This retains a nonzero supporting-fiber force `U_z` until the two
legitimate support bounds cancel its contribution. It does not assert
that the normal itself vanishes.

## 2. An exact inequality joining different stressed fibers

At a normalized fixed-offset hinge stress,

`c_i+kappa_i=sum_z eta_z lambda_zi`, `eta_z C_z=0`.

Multiply (2) by `eta_z` and sum the finitely many fibers. This gives

`sum_i (c_i+kappa_i) Psi_i
     >=sum_z eta_z t_z rho_z`.                                (3)

In the full joint Fritz--John system the same proof gives

`sum_i (alpha_0 c_i+r_i S_i) Psi_i
     >=sum_z eta_z t_z rho_z`.                                (4)

All moment bodies and all cap hinges are measured against the SAME
original mixed measure. Each hinge keeps one integer tilt over its
whole threshold integral. Thus these inequalities do not use the
invalid interchange of a tilt infimum with integration.

As one precisely limited consequence, if a normalized fixed-offset
stress has every `kappa_i=0`, then `c_i<=tau M`, coverage gives
`sum_z eta_z=sum_i c_i>=M`, and (3) yields

`tau Psi_D>=min_(eta_z>0)(t_z rho_z)`.                         (5)

When some `kappa_i` is positive, its term in (3) must be retained.
Likewise (4) retains both section weights and a possibly zero objective
multiplier. Neither a dimension-only positive lower bound on
`t_z rho_z` nor a bound on these budget multipliers is proved here.
Accordingly these are actual cross-fiber inequalities for the new
invariant, not a completed OC budget argument.
